answer.generated: Main-memory databases are preferred over traditional disk-based databases for real-time applications primarily because they mitigate the unpredictability associated with disk I/O operations, which can introduce significant variability in execution times. Even though data may reside in main memory, other factors such as lock contention and transaction aborts still contribute to execution time variance. Main-memory databases avoid these issues by eliminating the need for disk access, thus providing more consistent performance and reducing the likelihood of missing real-time constraints.
